sources.supports: deleteDataset validates the identifier, posts to delete_dataset/{dataset_id} with no body and no response schema, and awaits the request without returning a value. It is the only method of the module that declares no schema, so nothing is parsed out of the reply.

delete_dataset deletes an existing dataset and its parameter table carries dataset_id alone, marked required. The article states that deleting a dataset should also remove the dataset's values, and documents no response body. The documented failures are 400 for an invalid or missing dataset_id or for a dataset_id that is the Default dataset, 401 for authentication failure, and 403 for insufficient project or Test Data permissions or "Not an Enterprise license/subscription".

input_policy.notes: One identifier in the path and no request body at all, so every field beyond it is refused. TestRail's own refusal of the project's Default dataset is upstream and is reported as it arrives: which dataset is the default is instance state this boundary cannot know.

outer_result.notes: The method resolves with no value and the wrapper reports data: null, which matches TestRail documenting no response body. TestRail states the dataset's values go with it; the project's variables themselves remain, since a variable is an object of the project rather than of the dataset.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Send exactly one request. TestRail removes the dataset's values itself; the adapter never follows up with further calls to find or repair what the deletion removed.

parameters.semantics: The dataset to delete. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as the only path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.
